headline: High-risk filesystem and shell-capable AutoGPT paired with a non-networked sample repo creates prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure, while direct data leakage is limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, so if spring-integration-samples is used as shared content or copied into AutoGPT’s workspace, malicious instructions could be followed. The pair has no documented shared channel or provenance controls, so the pathway is plausible but not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, clipboard, or message queue
IF AutoGPT ingests files from spring-integration-samples as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable copy-paste of untrusted repo text into AutoGPT
Add provenance tags to any shared artifacts
Review any agent-generated instructions before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, but the profiles show no sensitive data classes, no shared workspace, and spring-integration-samples has network egress none. Without a documented shared data path, a leakage pathway is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace
IF sensitive files are introduced into that workspace
mitigations: Keep separate directories
Do not place secrets in shared folders
Restrict AutoGPT to a scratch workspace
Audit any file handoff before execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while spring-integration-samples is not runnable and exposes no write capabilities. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources or locks, so direct capability conflict is limited and mostly one-sided.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is mounted read-write alongside AutoGPT
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
mitigations: Mount spring-integration-samples read-only
Run AutoGPT in a separate working tree
Avoid concurrent writes to shared paths
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that a downstream workflow may treat as instructions, and spring-integration-samples is a sample repository that could be used as input material. Because no verification or critique step is documented, the pair can propagate errors if one agent’s output is consumed by the other without review.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is fed into AutoGPT for transformation
IF downstream automation accepts AutoGPT output without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on outputs
Compare outputs against source files
Limit AutoGPT to drafting only
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, residency, certification, or retention obligations are documented in either profile. AutoGPT is open-source and spring-integration-samples is a public sample repo, so the compliance mismatch pathway is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in this pair
Document data-class boundaries
Review deployment policies before use
